new.analysis:
Last week did exactly what it needed to: three identical sessions, pain 0/10, shin quiet, heart rate low, and no next-day grumble. That is the pattern we want to repeat and nudge, not reinvent.

The step this week is deliberately small. You go from 1.5 min of running to 2 min, with the walk break shortened to 1 min, and the Saturday session gets one extra round rather than a new structure. Longest continuous run moves from 1.5 min to 2 min, which is well inside the "add no more than 2 to 3 min" guardrail.

Keep the effort honest: easy breathing, able to talk, feet landing quietly. Your 6:45/km running splits last week were perfect for this phase, so do not try to run faster because the intervals are longer. The physio calf and hip work stays twice a week; those are doing real protective work for the shin.

The rule for the week stays simple. If the shin whispers during a run, stop and walk home; if it is louder the next morning, we repeat this week instead of adding next week. Four fully quiet weeks in a row is the gate before anything harder appears.

safetyCallouts.title: Stop if the shin speaks up.
safetyCallouts.body: Any pain during a run above 0 of 10, or soreness the next morning, means end the session and message your physio before the next run. We will repeat this week rather than add to it.
